title: Reading Poems Slowly
text:
Many readers find poetry difficult at first because the lines are short and the meaning is often hidden. A good poem rewards patience, since each word may carry more than one idea. Readers who slow down and read a poem aloud often notice its rhythm and sound.

Poets use images, metaphors and repetition to make their feelings clear without stating them directly. For example, a poet might compare grief to a heavy stone rather than simply saying that she is sad. Because of this, two readers may understand the same poem in different ways.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, why do many readers find poetry difficult at first?
options: The poems are always very long
The lines are short and the meaning is often hidden
Poems are written only in old languages
Poets never use sound or rhythm

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what do poets use to make their feelings clear?
What can be inferred about a reader who reads a poem aloud?
options: They may notice the rhythm and sound more easily
They are probably not interested in poetry
They understand the poem less than silent readers
They must already know the poet personally

questions.text: Why might two readers understand the same poem differently?
options: Because the poem has no real meaning
Because one reader has a shorter text
Because poets write different versions for each reader
Because the poem hides its ideas in images and comparisons

vocabulary.definition: not easy to see or understand at first
a regular pattern of sounds or beats in speech or music
words used to describe something as if it were something else
the act of using the same word or idea again

paragraph_translations: Muitos leitores acham a poesia difícil no início, porque os versos são curtos e o significado costuma estar oculto. Um bom poema recompensa a paciência, já que cada palavra pode carregar mais de uma ideia. Leitores que desaceleram e leem o poema em voz alta costumam perceber seu ritmo e sua sonoridade.

Poetas usam imagens, metáforas e repetição para deixar seus sentimentos claros sem dizê-los diretamente. Por exemplo, um poeta pode comparar o luto a uma pedra pesada em vez de simplesmente dizer que ela está triste. Por isso, dois leitores podem entender o mesmo poema de maneiras diferentes.
